properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 2019-12-26 to Coastal Petro Corp in Jenks Twp, Forest county. 78.57(a) - CONTROL, STORAGE AND DISPOSAL OF PRODUCTION FLUIDS - Operator failed to collect the brine and other fluids produced during operation, service and plugging of the well in a tank, pit or a series of pits or tanks, or other device approved by the Department or Operator discharged brine or other fluids on or into the ground or into waters of the Commonwealth.
properties.content:
Report Details
Operator: Coastal Petro Corp
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 2019-08-28
Violation Code: 78.57(a) - CONTROL, STORAGE AND DISPOSAL OF PRODUCTION FLUIDS - Operator failed to collect the brine and other fluids produced during operation, service and plugging of the well in a tank, pit or a series of pits or tanks, or other device approved by the Department or Operator discharged brine or other fluids on or into the ground or into waters of the Commonwealth.
Violation ID: 872755
Permit API: 053-30696
Unconventional: No
County: Forest
Municipality: Jenks Twp
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 2019-12-26
Comments: This site located west off Greeley Road north of junction with Francis Road in a forested area. Tank battery, two brine tanks and one oil tank in secondary containment, located along the access road. Marshall Wurst found this tank battery with a lined secondary containment containing a release of 2-3 bbls of crude oil on 8/23/2019. WQS Taylor inspected this site on 8/28/2019 and issued an NOV to Coastal Petro Corp. for the release of crude oil into the lined secondary containment. There was 1 1/2'-2' of crude oil/water in the secondary containment at the time of initial inspection. A follow-up inspection found that the liquid crude oil/water mix that was in the secondary containment has been removed. There is ice and snow covering most of the bottom of the secondary containment making it unclear as to the extent of the clean-up however the ice around the tanks appears to be clear and does not contain any residual oil contamination. An empty plastic 200 gallon is set in the secondary containment between the oil tank and first brine tank. A follow-up inspection will be completed when there is a thaw and the stone in the secondary containment can be inspected for contamination. This well to be transferred from Coastal Petro Corp. to Titusville Oil & Gas Associates Inc., application for the transfer of wells was sent in on 11/18/2019. Titusville Oil & Gas Associates, Inc. is to complete the clean-up at this site.

Unconventional: Yes
County: Greene

Inspection Date: 12/15/2023
Comments: On December 15, 2023, I conducted an inspection of the WL Hopkins Well Site. The inspection was conducted in response to a request made by an PA DEP OGI during an inspection conducted on 12/15/2023 (Sub-SAIR# 3660126). At the time of inspection, the following was observed:Act 9 Sign Installed, however the Operator of Record does not appear to be correct. The associated PPC plan and ER plan on site have not been updated to reflect the change in ownership. (Photo 11 and 12)The COASTAL Drill Rig was on site and connected to the well. The drill rig and associated equipment was not placed within secondary containment. (Photo 1)I observed fluid on the well pad surrounding the WL Hopkins 590312 Well and drill rig. I also observed fluid within the well cellar. I collected conductivity readings of the fluid on the well pad and within the cellar, which result in elevated conductivity readings. I also observed what appeared to be a light colored crystallin substance deposited on the well pad rock adjacent to the standing fluid. The crystallin substance appears to be salt which suggest that the fluid has been on site long enough to begin evaporation. The amount of fluid on the well pad appeared to be greater than 42 gallons. At the time of inspection, the Department was not previously notified by the Operator of a release of fluid to the well pad. (Photo 2 thru 10)While I was on site, I contacted Operator representative Kevin Wright (CONSOL/Leatherwood) to relay my observations related to the fluid release and recommend that the Operator being remediation immediately. Mr. Wright indicated that the Operator added brine to the well to kill the well on 11/15/2023.I am requesting clarification of the activity, date and time of when the fluid was added to the well bore and all information/inspections related to the monitoring of the well between 11/15/2023 and 12/15/2023. I am also requesting clarification of the source of the fluid added to the well bore on or around 11/15/2023.Violation are being issued for the release (78a.54, 78a57(a), 91.34(a), SWMA 301, 78a66(b)1,78a(b)1(i), 78a66(b)1(ii), 78a66(b)(2), 91.33(a) and 91.33(b).Violations are being issued for the failure to develop a site specific PPC plan and ER Plan. 78a55(a), 78a55(b), 78a55(c). 78a55(h).Violations are being issued for the failure to properly update the Act 9 Sign (78a55(i)(4)(D)(III).Violations are being issued for the failure to install secondary containment. (78a64(a))

properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 9/02/2026 to SCORPIO ENERGY INC in Howe Township, Forest county. 78.53 - EROSION AND SEDIMENT CONTROL - Operator failed to design, implement and maintain best management practices and an erosion and sediment control plan in accordance with 25 Pa. Code Chapter 102, during and after earthmoving or soil disturbing activities, including the activities related to siting, drilling, completing, producing, servicing and plugging, constructing, utilizing and restoring the site and access road.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: SCORPIO ENERGY INC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 9/02/2026
Violation Code: 78.53 - EROSION AND SEDIMENT CONTROL - Operator failed to design, implement and maintain best management practices and an erosion and sediment control plan in accordance with 25 Pa. Code Chapter 102, during and after earthmoving or soil disturbing activities, including the activities related to siting, drilling, completing, producing, servicing and plugging, constructing, utilizing and restoring the site and access road.
Violation ID: 8287772
Permit API: 053-31161
Unconventional: No
County: Forest
Municipality: Howe Township
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 9/02/2026
Comments: This site is undergoing construction for the development of a conventional well. The drilling permit and E and S Plan are posted at the entrance of the location. There was no activity on the location at the time of this inspection. The template for the site and access road has been completed. The gathering lines for this well have been buried within the template of the road. Stone has not yet been applied to any portion of the road or well site. The E and S Plan that was prepared for this site is inadequate as it does not account for all surface waters of the Commonwealth that converge with the earth disturbance associated with the construction of this well site and the access road that leads to it. In addition, the site and access road have been excavated significantly below the natural grade, therefore, watercourses that were likely below the surface prior to construction are now present at the surface and are not accounted for in the E and S Plan. Due to the insufficient plan and construction practices, the BMPs that have been installed are insufficient and are promoting stormwater to become concentrated and directed into waters of the Commonwealth. Numerous waters of the Commonwealth are also being removed from their natural channel and redirected.The ditches along the access road do not consist of a durable material, nor have they been stabilized to account for the flow of water running through them and have become significantly eroded due to the volume and velocity of stormwater and surface water. Aside from the lack of stabilization measures in the ditch, the roadside banks and perimeter of the location (that do not appear to require any additional excavation) have also not yet been stabilized. No perimeter BMPs (such as silt sock) have been installed for minimizing the amount of sediment leaving the un-stabilized areas of earth disturbance. The culverts that have been installed at the intermittent streams have been poorly installed. There is excessive excavation at the inlets and outlets of these water features resulting in sediment entering the stream channels. The E and S Plan does not account for headwall protection at these culverts, therefore, the disturbed earth near the inlets and outlets is vulnerable to scouring and erosion into the water channel. Improper installation and the lack of energy dissipators at the outlets of the installed cross-pipes that are conveying stormwater is resulting in scouring at the outlets of these culverts and increasing the amount of accelerated erosion and sedimentation. Since no stone has been placed on the road, recent traffic on the road template after rain events has caused the template to become soft and appreciably rutted in spots. This has allowed stormwater, and in some areas, the flow from a watercourse to flow onto the road template. As a result of these deficiencies, there has been accelerated erosion across the earth disturbance associated with the construction of the access road and well site. Significant amounts of sediment have discharged into and remain accumulated in spring seeps and unnamed tributary of Hastings Run.In addition to the E and S deficiencies, due to the abundance of shallow ground water at the site, the use of pits for temporary containment or permanent encapsulation of cuttings or any residual waste from this well in a pit would not satisfy the requirements outlined in Chapter 78.56(a)(8), unless Scorpio Energy can demonstrate otherwise to the Department in advance of lining the pit.The deficiencies noted above also apply to the first well location (Well Site 56) and the access road getting to that site. Corrective action should be applied to both sites in order to remediate the noted violations and to return to compliance.

Comments: I spoke with Brendon Logan (Chief) on site. He explained the compressor unit caught fire on January 16, 2021. I did not see any Post Construction Stormwater Management (PCSM) controls in place. The PCSM Plan includes rock spreaders and an infiltration berm that are in place under the snow. Containment structures are intact; I did not observe any leaks or other deficiencies today. There is no standing liquid on site today; it's all frozen (snow, ice). Air temp 22F JLP

Comments: On 11/30/2023, a routine complete inspection was conducted at the Stech F69 well. The following was observed:The well and operator's information were posted onsite (Photos 1, 2).The wellhead, production equipment, and production tank were in generally good condition. Some corrosion noted, loose wires/equipment near wellhead (Photos 3-6). Tank fluids high - I recommend pumping fluid out and placing lid on tank (Photo 7).Silt fence in the woods below production tank. I recommend ensuring that no sediment from the site washes downslope towards the tributary below (Photo 8).The access road was in poor condition leading the whole way to the site from the main road (Photos 9-25 with specific locations). Several areas displayed lack of maintenence and drainage concerns seen by pooling, potholes, channelization, and accelerated erosion. Culverts that run under the road leading to tributary to Pigeon Creek appeared to require clean out and outlet protection - erosion at outlets. There was a section of the access road closer to the entrance gate that displayed undercutting and failure along the guardrail. The integrity of the access road appeared jeopardized and may progress with repeated rain events and heavy truck traffic. The road does not display a safe way for emergency vehicles to navigate in case of emergency at the wellsite.Observations communicated to operator via phone on 11/30/23.Due to the poor condition of the access road and lack of maintenance, violations of 102.4(b)1, 102.11(a), 78.53, and 102.22(a)2ii are being issued.

Comments: Inspection record #2860077 submitted on 3-28-19 was submitted in error. This inspection supersedes inspection record #2860077. At time of inspection well appears equipped for production. Department observes a thick, light yellow substance coming from brine tank. This substance appears to be petroleum based. This substance appears to be leaking from the top of the brine tank, where the piping from the well head attaches. This substance flows down the side of the brine tank (photo #1), and has ponded in two areas at the base of the brine tank (photo #2). Department contacted operator rep Josh Martz by phone from site. Mr. Martz states a well tender will be sent to the site. 14:42- Mr. Martz contacted Department by phone, left message. Mr. Martz states a release of approx 5-6 gal of crude oil occurred. Mr. Martz states water forced the tank to overflow. Mr. Martz states the tank has been emptied of water and that he will report the release to the DEP emergency line. 14:59- Department received spill report. This report states 5-6 gal of crude oil was released on 3-28-19. 16:32- Mr. Martz contacted Department by phone, left message. Mr. Martz states surface clean up has been completed. Mr. Martz states the crude oil will be removed from the tank next week. Mr. Martz states after crude oil is removed, the tank will be cleaned up, impacted soil will be removed, area under tank will be checked and impacted soil, if any, removed. Mr. Martz also states he will provide photos of cleanup to Department and will keep Department updated on status of site. Violations are being issued for failure to collect brine or other fluids, failure to control and dispose of fluids, and for disposal of residual waste inconsistent with the rules and regulations of DEP. A follow up inspection will be conducted at a later date.

Comments: On 03/22/19 - 10:30: Lower Reno 4A 121-44422 was observed pumping. The production line from this well is buried and travels underground to a separator located near Lower Reno 1 A 121-44463. From the separator, the oil line is buried and travels down gradient to the production tanks. The brine line runs on the surface down gradient. The fittings on the brine line from the separator are showing signs of corrosion and are occasionally dripping onto the ground. It appears there has been a previous discharge in the area by the appearance of the dead vegetation. The brine line was followed down gradient and observed discharging at 41.421803 N, -79.768843 W. At the spot the discharge was occurring the line was separated at a hose nipple. There is a large area of dead vegetation at the discharge location. When the well was pumping a substantial amount of fluid was observed discharging. On this date a sample could not be collected, and further investigation will take place. 03/27/19 - 09:45 The area where the flow line was previously discharging was inspected and found to be discharging. A sample was collected (0641-119). The flow rate during sampling was much slower then observed on 03/22/19. After the sample was collected it was observed that no wells were currently pumping. The operator was called (Harry Rhodes) and notified of the violation. The Department will meet with the operator on 04/02/19. The operator was advised that he should shut the lease down to cease the discharge. Violations are noted.

Code §§ 78a.55 – 78a.58 and 78a.60 – 78a.63.
Violation ID: 8268742
Permit API: 059-26446
Unconventional: Yes
County: Greene
Municipality: Washington Township
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 3/27/2026
Comments: On 03/27/2026, an incident inspection was conducted at the Anthony Petraitis Well Site following receipt of a spill report, submitted to the Department on 03/26/2026 (CTS 396174). I was accompanied by Water Quality Specialist Laura Grada (PA DEP), EQT representative Doug Oberdorf, and SPSI representative Billy Wade. SPSI was on site for remediation.EQT reported a spill of approximately 5 gallons of production fluid from a flow line. They reported that SPSI was on site, the release was contained, and no waterways were affected.EQT indicated on site that they intend to remediate per Act 2 guidelines. The fluid was on the pad, underneath the pad liner; the pad liner was above the pad substrate and contained pea gravel overtop of the liner. When the Department arrived on site, SPSI indicated that 1 vac box was around half full of the removed fluids; this was the only box that was used, and none were removed from site full.The following was observed during inspection:SPSI had vac trucks on site and were in the process of remediation (Photo 1).The spill was located around Gas Production Unit (GPU) 6H. The leak originated at the elbow joint of the associated GPU piping. The spilled fluid reached the underside of the pad liner; the fluid was also pooling on top of the pad liner, within the pea gravel (Photos 2-5).Several sumps were dug on both sides of the spill origin at GPU 6H and its associated elbow joint within the piping. Conductivity readings were obtained within the soil and water at the sump locations. The sump located 15 feet from the elbow joint yielded a conductivity reading of 1835 uS/cm within the soil (Photo 6). The sump 30 feet from the elbow joint yielded a conductivity reading of 644 uS/cm within the soil (Photo 7). The sump located 10 feet from the elbow yielded a water conductivity reading of 13.04 mS/cm and a soil reading of 6.18 mS/cm (Photos 8, 9). The sump located 35 feet from the elbow yielded a conductivity reading of 2.86 mS/cm within the soil this reading was unable to be replicated; the operator will monitor this location (Photo 10). properties.content:
Report Details

Unconventional: Yes
County: Bradford

Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 2019-09-09
Comments: On 09/07/19 at 1130 hrs, Steve Moyer notified Phone Duty Officer (Andrew Hobbins)reporting that two puddles on the GU-J-Pad well pad surface tested high for conductivity while removing containment. The first puddle measured approximately 11mS/cm and the other puddle measured 3-4 mS/cm. Mr. Moyer reported that containment cleanup was ongoing, but currently the impacted pad surface is limited to a 30 foot by 40 foot area near the well heads, and a second area is still being investigated is ranging up to 7 mS/cm conductivity and is roughly 50 feet by 60 feet.  Mr. Moyer attributed the high conductivity to a hole somewhere in the containment liner, but no holes were found. A vac truck removed the puddles from the pad surface. Resource Environmental was contracted to delineate the impacted area and do remediation work. SWN finished their drill out and was currently setting up to hook up flow lines for the new wells. No waterways or stormwater/infiltration areas were affected. On September 09, 2019 Department representative Jared Jacobini (Water Quality Specialist) conducted a site inspection in response to an incident reported on 09/07/19 by Steve Moyer (Southwestern Energy (SWN) Regulatory Supervisor) at SWNs WELL PAD J. Also present for the inspection was production supervisor Mike Deming of SWN. When I arrived onsite, the operator had scraped excavated impacted soils near the well cellars and towards the low area on the pad near the level spreader (Photo # 1-8). The excavated soil had been removed and placed into seven roll offs and was being removed during the inspection. At the time of inspection, the volume and cause of the release was not know but was still being investigated with anticipation of pursuing Act 2. The pad surface was screened with a soil probe conductivity meter and a handheld conductivity meter throughout the impacted and excavated area, puddles, and outside of the pad below the level spreader. In one location that did not appear to have been excavated, the soil conductivity was 3.43 mS/ cm (Photo # 9-10). In a second location beyond the well heads along the western pad border a puddle exhibiting a sheen had a conductivity of 1,126 µS/cm (Photo # 12). Mike Deming said that he would have the area were soil conductivity was high scraped up and the location of puddled water vacuumed up. This release should be remediated in accordance with Chapter 78a66(c). As a result of the presence of a pollutional substance discovered on the pad surface the following violations are being cited.

Violation ID: 8271274
Permit API: 051-24570
Unconventional: Yes
County: Fayette
Municipality: Redstone Township

Inspection Date: 4/13/2026
Comments: On April 13, 2026, the Department conducted an inspection in response to a complaint (CTS-396434) at the Ritter well site in Redstone Township, Fayette County. The purpose of this inspection was to conduct further on-site review. An Erosion and Sedimentation Control General Permit (ESCGP) for this site was terminated on July 10, 2017.The following was observed during the inspection:The Act 9 sign is installed at the entrance of Tree Farm road and is not obscured from view by vegetation, in an accordance with 78a.55 (photo 1). Tree Farm Road is a township gravel road that connects to the site access road. The Emergency Response Plan (ERP) is on site (photo 2). Eight gas wells are onsite that appear to be equipped for production. Well 5H is equipped with a well tag with no observable evidence of a fluid leak to the ground around it (photo 17). The well and operator's information are displayed and visible on this well tag, as required by OGA 3211(g) and OGA 3211(h).The production tanks and the surrounding secondary containment appear to be sound at the time of inspection. The GPU units are not equipped with secondary containment. However, the gas wells on site were drilled prior to the promulgation of 78a. No evidence of a fluid leak, such as staining, was observed on the ground around the GPU units (photos 16 and 18).The access road and well pad appear to be stable at the time of inspection with no observable accelerated erosion and sedimentation (photos 4 and 19).The severe accelerated erosion and sedimentation remains downslope of the well pad on Tree Farm Road (photos 10-13). The Department observed a rock-lined stormwater channel along the access road, which is located upslope of Tree Farm Road. This rock-lined stormwater channel appears to be in need of maintenance, as it appears to be nearly level with the access road (photo 6). Vegetation that appears to be flattened by recent stormwater washout was observed downslope of the rock-lined stormwater channel and access road (photo 5). An erosion channel obscured by vegetation was found within the well site boundary upslope of the most severely eroded portion of Tree Farm Road (photo 14). This erosion channel appears to pose the potential to encourage channelized stormwater flow downslope to Tree Farm Road.Based on observations from this inspection, violations are being issued for failure to conduct long-term maintenance on Post-Construction Stormwater Management Best Management Practices (PCSM BMPs), which appear to be discharging excess stormwater to Tree Farm Road and resulting in accelerated erosion and sedimentation.Transmittal of this inspection report was delayed due to an IT error.

Violation ID: 8240285

Unconventional: Yes

Inspection Date: 6/30/2025
Comments: On June 30, 2025, the DEP conducted an Incident Inspection of Olympus Energy's Porter Well Pad located in Allegheny Township, Westmoreland County following a spill that was reported to the DEP hotline on 6/27/2025 at 2:37 pm.The spill report stated that at 1:15 pm on 6/27/2025, over 5 gallons of a produced water (Photo 12), fresh water, and frack chemicals (Photos 13-15) mixture was released on containment and on the gravel well pad at the Porter Well site.Accompanying during today's inspection is Olympus representative Laura Karosic.At the time of this inspection, the DEP observed an Act 9 Sign posted at the access road entrance with all required information posted on it. In the on-site mailbox, the DEP observed both an Emergency Response Plan and Preparedness, Prevention, and Contingency Plan, that had all required components.At the time of this inspection, zipper frack operations were being conducted on 2 Utica wells with 57 out of 153 fracks remaining.At the time of this inspection, Ms. Karosic stated that a hose connected to the blender ruptured spraying the mixture on and off containment, however no Waters of the Commonwealth were impacted. At the time of this inspection, the DEP observed the area of the graveled pad where this incident occurred to be adjacent to a fresh water impoundment located on site. The graveled well pad in this incident appeared to be scraped, the ground in this area was observed to be brown and muddy in comparison to the dry and gray graveled well pad surrounding this area. Ms. Karosic stated that 2-4 inches of the well pad in this incident area was scraped and vacuums were used to suck up any puddles of fluid. The secondary containment where this incident occurred appeared to be clean and dry.At the time of this inspection, the DEP observed 3 clamshell dumpsters on site, 2 were full of contaminated material and the 3rd will be filled with any remaining contaminated material once Moody arrives to conduct further remediation efforts.At the time of this inspection, the DEP utilized a conductivity meter to screen the graveled well pad. The DEP collected readings of 8.30 mS, 3.07 mS and 2.20 mS in the incident area and 8.21 mS underneath/at the base of the clean water impoundment. The area outside of this incident area where the ground was not scraped was also screened and the readings collected in that area was comparable to the background reading of 0.333 mS collected in vegetation by the Act 9 Sign. At the time of this inspection, the DEP notified Ms. Karosic of the elevated soil conductivity readings in the incident area and underneath the fresh water impoundment. Ms. Karosic stated that fracking operations is scheduled to commence between July 10-11, 2025, then the fresh water impoundment will be removed and remediation can be conducted in the area where the impoundment was located. The DEP recommends the Operator promptly remediate the release in accordance with 78a.66(c)(2).At the time of this inspection, Ms. Karosic stated that at this time they estimate that the quantity of the release is between 1 and 3 barrels and that they anticipate following Act 2 protocol for the clean up. At the time of this inspection, the DEP observed SDSs for all chemicals on site and included in the release mixture to be located in the on site trailer. Based on today's inspection, violations shall be issued for the 1-3 barrel release of produced water, fresh water, and fracking chemicals on the graveled well pad.The Operator is requested to submit a written response within 15 days of the receipt of this report. This response should include an incident report, a timeline, a plan for remediation of the violations and how the Operator quantified the amount released. The Operator will need to follow Act 2 guidelines as set by 78a.66(c)(2) and assess the impacts to the Water of the Commonwealth from the release.

Comments: On November 26, 2024, the Department conducted an inspection in response to a referral from OGI Charles Reaggle (IR 3864611 on 10/18/2024). OGI Charles Reaggle requested that a WQS follow up because of observed fluid dripping from both annulus wings. Well appears to be equipped for production. Site is well vegetated.Well tag requirement fulfilled with API number present on production tank. Well posting for Big Dog Energy does not appear to be correct Operator. In IR 3864611, the Department noted that the well transferred Operators from Big Dog Energy to Dorso LP, however the well has since transferred again to Apollo Resources as of October 30, 2024. The Department recommends Apollo Resources fulfill the well posting requirement in accordance with OGA3211(G).Drip still observed coming from the annulus. Specific conductivity was measured inside the annulus (7.62 mS / 7,620 uS), in the soil below the annulus (1.161 mS / 1,161 uS), and three background points of the soil surrounding the site (0.1805 mS / 180.5 uS), (0.1524 mS / 152.4 uS), (0.262 mS / 262 uS). These measurements of specific conductivity indicate that a release of brine has occurred from the annulus. The Department recommends the Operator repair the annulus to prevent further release. The Department recommends the Operator remove all impacted soil/material and properly disposing of the soil/material.Production tank on site and appears to be structurally sound at this time. Violations are being issued for release of production fluid to the ground. Previously issued violations in IR 3864611 by OGI Charles Reaggle are being evaluated under enforcement ID 435756.The Operator is requested to submit a written response within seven (7) days of the receipt of this report. This written response should include an incident report, a timeline of remedial measures, and plan for remediation of the spill or release. The Department is requesting how the Operator quantified the amount spilled. The Department also requests the waste manifest from the site remediation be submitted upon receipt.

Report Details
Inspection Client: EQT ARO LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 3/11/2025
Violation Code: 78a57(a) - CONTROL, STORAGE AND DISPOSAL OF PRODUCTION FLUIDS - Operator failed to collect brine and other fluids produced during operation of the well in a tank, series of tanks, or other device approved by the Department for subsequent disposal or reuse.
Violation ID: 8224390
Permit API: 027-21548
Unconventional: Yes
County: Centre
Municipality: Snow Shoe Township
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 3/11/2025
Comments: Rick Hall of EQT called at 1210 and reported an unknown amount of brine was released at the COP Tract 231 Pad A on March 11, 2025 due to a brine dump line failure.I conducted a site inspection on March 11, 2025. EQT representative Zac Subra was onsite and explained that there are 3 dump lines that run to the produced fluids tank farm. These lines are partially above and below ground (picture 2). The far left line in the picture runs from the compressor unit to the produced fluids tank farm. The other two lines run from the GPUs to the produced fluids tank farm. One is a primary main line and the other is a secondary line. According to Mr. Subra, the lease operator alternates the lines during the winter months. The lease operator discovered a leak today coming from the secondary brine line. The leak was discovered where the brine line meets gravel/soil. Standing fluids were observed in the release area with a conductivity reading of >4.00 mS/cm (picture 4). According to Mr. Subra, no fluids remain in the produced fluids tanks.EQT has contacted Tobias Machining and Welding for site remediation. Tobias staff were onsite digging potholes to try and find the buried dump lines and testing those potholes for elevated conductance. Laureen Butters of Penn E and R was onsite conducting the soil screenings. Please note, exposed soils where the release occurred and in the potholes, showed sandy soils.During my inspection several potholes were dug and tested for elevated conductance. In addition, several holes were hand dug underneath the above ground lines to help delineate the impacted area. Based off my observation a section of soils were impacted approximately 40 feet in length underneath the above ground lines. According to Mr. Subra, a vacuum truck was enroute to the site. EQT is having site meeting with production staff on the morning of March 12, 2025 to determine what production equipment can be dismantled and removed in order to proceed with site remediation. I screened along the wooded edge of the well pad adjacent to the brine spill and found no elevated conductivity readings. In addition, I screened along the edge of Million Dollar road and wooded area and found no elevated conductivity readings. Violations have been cited for the brine release. Given the unknown amount of brine released, the Department recommends that the operator pursues Act 2 for site remediation.
